metadata.llm_reason: Candidate is a knowledge_reference on Dynamic Timestamp Allocation (DTA) for deadlock detection in 2PL algorithms. It is semantically distinct from peer candidates (which address serializability proofs, abort classification, and serial ordering in OCC systems) and from existing skills (which cover parallel execution and cache eviction). DTA is a timestamp-based deadlock detection technique specific to pessimistic locking (2PL), not optimistic concurrency control. The support evidence (5.4 Lower Isolation Levels 6.1 Workloads) validates the scalability constraints and critical section bottleneck cautions. No conflict evidence exists. This should be persisted as a new foundational knowledge reference.
